title: Regional Preference Horizon: latency-first failover + capacity-aware pinning
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We see occasional cross-region flaps where clients are bounced between regions during short-lived spikes. That increases tail latency and cache churn and occasionally violates our 99p latency SLOs for some customers. Goal: implement a 'Regional Preference Horizon' policy that prefers low-latency regions but pins a requesting principal to the chosen region for a short horizon, and that gracefully fails over when capacity or latency deteriorates. Key constraints: preserve KV cache locality where possible, avoid long pins that hamper load balancing, integrate with existing circuit-breaker signals and token-shedder, and keep policy deterministic for debugging. This ticket designs and implements the scoring, pin/horizon semantics, and capacity-aware fallback behavior. It should also include experiments to validate SLO improvement and cost impact.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 99th-percentile region-to-client latency for pinned flows improves or is stable during canary compared to baseline (<= 5% regression allowed)
2) On simulated regional capacity degradation, 95% of pinned requests failover within the configured failover window and obey circuit-breaker rules (no more than 1% unexpected retries)
3) Prefix/KV cache hit-rate for pinned flows degrades by less than 10% during normal traffic vs baseline
4) Dashboard + alerting created: pin_count, pin_horizon_seconds, failover_count, preemptive_shed_count, regional_score_distribution
5) Automated e2e test shows deterministic pin assignment for identical principal+route fingerprints across 1000 requests
technical_notes: Scoring function (proto): score(region) = alpha * p50_latency(region, client) + beta * (1 / available_capacity_fraction) + gamma * region_penalty_if_evicting

We will normalize latency to a 0..1 range using historical p50 for that client region pair. Capacity term uses smoothed available GPU slots / total slots per pool. Default weights: alpha=0.6, beta=0.35, gamma=0.05 (tunable via remote config)

Pin semantics: once a region is selected, assign a soft pin for H seconds (default H=300). Soft pin means: primary routing goes to pinned region; requests may be hedged if pinned region latency exceeds dynamic threshold for >3 consecutive samples or circuit breaker opens
Hysteresis: add an aging factor so pin strength decays linearly to zero between H and 3H seconds unless reinforced by traffic from same principal

Circuit breakers: integrate with existing region-level CB that trips on sustained p99 latency or error-rate or on token-queue-depth thresholds. When CB trips, pinned flows mark region as degraded and re-solve the scoring function excluding that region for the next 60s

Load shedding: use token-bucket budget per-principal per-region to enforce short-term shedding when chosen region load approaches critical capacity. Shed decisions annotated in trace for observability

KV cache note: propagate pin metadata (region id + horizon expiry) in request headers so downstream caches can apply short-lived affinity for hot KV entries. Include TTL guards to prevent cache pollution
Determinism: fingerprint uses (customer_id || route_id || client_ip_prefix/ASN). Provide metric to surface cases where fingerprint leads to tie-breaking randomness
Fallback: if all candidate regions are filtered by CB or capacity, escalate to cross-tier fallback (burst to shared pools) and increment failover_count metric
API/Config: expose per-route config: prefer_locality (bool), default_horizon_seconds, max_hard_pin_seconds, weights (alpha,beta,gamma), max_hedge_rate
Compatibility: must work with Hosted and Dedicated pools; ensure private deployment has config surface but defaults preserved
rollout_plan: Dev: implement scoring + pin state machine behind flag, unit tests, and sim harness (2 weeks)
Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on staging cluster with synthetic client profiles measuring latency and cache hit rates (1 week)
Beta: enable for 5 customers in Hosted (opt-in) for 2 weeks, observe SLOs and cost; iterate on weights
Gradual: ramp to 25% traffic, then 50% over two weeks if metrics stable
Full: enable as route default for new routes; provide toggle in Console for existing routes
metrics_and_dashboards: regional_score_distribution: histogram of chosen region scores per route
pin_horizon_active: current number of active pins
pin_failover_count: count of pins that failed over due to CB or capacity
kv_cache_hit_rate_pinned: cache hit rate for requests with active pin

2026-03-08 - Design (Marta Lopez): Console needs a per-route control and an explanation tooltip. Mockups uploaded to Figma link.
2026-03-11 - Security (Liam O'Rourke): Reviewed header propagation approach; flagged need to avoid PII in fingerprinting. Added tasks to sanitize customer_id before fingerprinting.

last_decision: Use soft pins with a 5-minute default horizon, scoring that biases latency over capacity but includes a capacity term for preemptive shedding; integrate with region CBs and add explicit per-route opt-out
notes_for_QA: Simulate regional outage by reducing available_capacity_fraction to 0.2 and assert failover_count increments and that requests retry no more than once
Verify header TTL and ensure no PII is propagated in the fingerprint header
Run cache-hit A/B comparing pinned vs non-pinned flows over 24h synthetic workload
